question.problem: For the function $f(x,y)=\frac{{y}^{2}-{x}^{2}}{\sqrt{y}},$ evaluate $\frac{∂f}{∂y}$ at the point $(3,1).$
question.worked_solution:
We differentiate the given function with respect to $y,$ treating all other variables as constants. 

First, we use the quotient rule:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂}{∂y}(\frac{{y}^{2}-{x}^{2}}{\sqrt{y}}) & =\frac{\frac{∂}{∂y}({y}^{2}-{x}^{2})\cdot \sqrt{y}-({y}^{2}-{x}^{2})\cdot \frac{∂}{∂y}(\sqrt{y})}{{(\sqrt{y})}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{(2y\cdot \sqrt{y}-({y}^{2}-{x}^{2})\cdot \frac{1}{2\sqrt{y}})}{y} \\  & =\frac{(\frac{4{y}^{2}+{x}^{2}-{y}^{2}}{2\sqrt{y}})}{y} \\  & =\frac{{x}^{2}+3{y}^{2}}{2y\sqrt{y}}\end{aligned}
$$

 

Finally, we evaluate the partial derivative at the point $(3,1):$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x}{|}_{(3,1)} & =\frac{{3}^{2}+3(1)^{2}}{2(1)\sqrt{1}} \\  & =\frac{9+3}{2} \\  & =6\end{aligned}
$$
